sets.ref: published, OSU Ximera Electromagnetics (electrical length): a 7.5 cm line is a quarter wavelength (90°) at 1 GHz; λ = c/f = 299792458/1e9 = 0.299792458 m (PIC Wire: 11.80 in at 1 GHz and 100 % VOP), ℓ = 90/360 · 0.299792458 = 0.0749481 m

published, Steer Microwave and RF Design II section 2.2, first example: ℓ = 10 cm with β = 30 rad/m is 3 rad = 171.9° = 0.477 λ; the frequency of that β in air is f = 30·299792458/(2π) = 1.431404e9 Hz, λ = 0.2094395 m, ℓ = 3/(2π) · 0.2094395 = 0.1 m

published (VF), Ellingson Electromagnetics Vol. 1 section 3.10: RG-59 with ε_r = 2.25 has about 67 % of c, VF = 1/√2.25 = 0.666667; half-wave at 100 MHz: λ = 299792458 · 0.666667/1e8 = 1.998616 m, ℓ = 180/360 · 1.998616 = 0.999308 m
hand, quarter-wave section for the 2 m band in 0.66 coax: λ = 299792458 · 0.66/1.45e8 = 1.364573 m, ℓ = 1.364573/4 = 0.341143 m
